=== pick-from-canvas
     1	---
     2	title: "Pick from Canvas"
     3	description: "Click a colour in the preview to centre an adjustment clip's qualifier on it, instead of finding it on the range strips."
     4	---
     5	
     6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
     7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
     8	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
     9	
    10	Pick from Canvas aims a [qualifier](/color/qualifiers/) at a colour you can see. You click the picture and the ranges centre on that colour, so you don't have to find it on the strips by hand. The [chroma key](/effects/chroma-key/#pick-from-canvas) has an eyedropper of its own, with the same name.
    11	
    12	<AtAGlance
    13	  where="Color tab ▸ Qualifier ▸ Pick from Canvas"
    14	  tools={['set_video', 'set_action_end']}
    15	  needs="Every selected clip must be an adjustment clip."
    16	/>
    17	
    18	<Shot
    19	  name="05h-clip-qualifier.inspector"
    20	  alt="The Qualifier section of the Color tab, with Hue ticked at Centre 25°, Width 30° and Soft 15°, Saturation ticked at Low 0.15, High 1.00 and Soft 0.05, Luma unticked, and the Pick from Canvas button beside a ticked Show Selection."
    21	/>
    22	
    23	## Pick a colour
    24	
    25	<Steps>
    26	
    27	1. Select the [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/), and move the playhead to a frame that shows the colour.
    28	
    29	2. In the [Color tab](/color/color-tab/), open the **Qualifier** section and press **Pick from Canvas**. The pointer becomes a crosshair over the preview, and a hint reads "Click to pick the colour to qualify · Esc to cancel".
    30	
    31	3. Click the colour in the preview.
    32	
    33	</Steps>
    34	
    35	The ranges move to that colour, and the pick ends. It's one undo step, named Qualifier.
    36	
    37	Frame Job reads the colour from the picture behind the adjustment clip, at the playhead. The clip's own grade and every layer in front of it are left out. So the colour you get is the one the qualifier will really test, even after your grade has changed how it looks, and clicking a title on top samples what's underneath it.
    38	
    39	Turn on [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/) to check what the pick caught.
    40	
    41	## What a pick sets
    42	
    43	| Range | If it was off | If it was on |
    44	| --- | --- | --- |
    45	| **Hue** | Turns on, centred on the colour, 30° wide with 15° softness. | Moves its centre to the colour. |
    46	| **Saturation** | Turns on, centred on the colour's saturation, 0.3 wide with softness 0.1. | Moves to centre on the colour's saturation. |
    47	| **Luma** | Stays off. | Moves to centre on the colour's brightness. |
    48	
    49	A range that was already on keeps its width and softness, so you can set how wide you want a range and then pick again to move it. **Invert** and **Blur** don't change.
    50	
    51	If you click a near-grey, there's no real hue to aim at, so **Hue** turns off. A near-grey here is a colour whose strongest and weakest channels are less than 0.06 apart, on a scale of 0 to 1. **Saturation** still turns on and centres, which is how you pick the greys in a picture.
    52	
    53	**Saturation** and **Luma** stay inside 0 to 1. A range that would cross either end is shifted back inside at its full width, so it's no longer centred on the colour, but the colour stays inside it.
    54	
    55	## Pick inside an action
    56	
    57	With an [action](/motion/select-an-action/) selected, the picked ranges go to the action's end state instead of the clip, as any qualifier control does. The width and softness a range keeps are the ones the section is showing. Clicking a near-grey takes **Hue** out of the end state rather than turning it off, so if the clip itself has **Hue** on, it stays on. See [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/).
    58	
    59	## Cancel a pick
    60	
    61	Press <kbd>Esc</kbd>, or press **Pick from Canvas** again. Changing the selection cancels the pick too. Nothing in the qualifier changes.
    62	
    63	A click in the area around the picture beeps and leaves the pick armed, so you can click again.
    64	
    65	## Good to know
    66	
    67	- Only one canvas mode can be armed at a time. Arming Pick from Canvas cancels any other, such as the chroma key's eyedropper or a [Zoom to Region](/motion/zoom-to-region/) drag, and arming one of those cancels a pick.
    68	- If the playhead isn't on the adjustment clip, no layers are left out, so you sample the frame as it's drawn.
    69	- [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/) and [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/) don't change what you sample. A pick reads the real picture, whatever the preview is showing.
    70	- With several adjustment clips selected, Frame Job samples behind the first and writes the same ranges to all of them.
    71	- In an HDR (HLG) project, a pick reads the HLG values, which are what the qualifier tests.
    72	- If the selection changes while Frame Job is sampling, it beeps and changes nothing.
    73	
    74	## With an agent
    75	
    76	No agent tool clicks the canvas. An agent writes the ranges itself with `set_video`, or with `set_action_end` for an action's end state. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/).
    77	
    78	## Related
    79	
    80	- [Qualifiers](/color/qualifiers/)
    81	- [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/)
    82	- [Adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/)
    83	- [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/)
    84	- [Chroma Key](/effects/chroma-key/)
=== show-selection
     1	---
     2	title: "Show Selection"
     3	description: "See in grey exactly which pixels an adjustment clip's qualifier picks, so you can tune its ranges before you judge the grade."
     4	---
     5	
     6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
     7	
     8	Show Selection replaces the preview with a grey picture of what a [qualifier](/color/qualifiers/) picks. It shows you which pixels an adjustment clip's grade reaches, so you can tune the ranges without guessing from the graded picture.
     9	
    10	<AtAGlance
    11	  menu="View ▸ Show Selection"
    12	  where="Color tab ▸ Qualifier ▸ Show Selection"
    13	  tools="render_frame"
    14	  needs="An adjustment clip selected."
    15	/>
    16	
    17	## Turn it on
    18	
    19	Select an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/), then tick **Show Selection** in the **Qualifier** section of the [Color tab](/color/color-tab/), or choose **View ▸ Show Selection**. Do the same again to turn it off. It's off to begin with and has no keyboard shortcut.
    20	
    21	The checkbox and the menu item are the same switch, and the menu item has a checkmark while it's on. The menu item is dimmed while Show Selection is off and no adjustment clip is selected.
    22	
    23	## Read the picture
    24	
    25	| The preview shows | What it means |
    26	| --- | --- |
    27	| White | The clip's grade applies in full here. |
    28	| Black | The grade doesn't touch this pixel. |
    29	| Grey | The grade applies in part, as it does across a range's soft edge. |
    30	
    31	The picture is the selection as the clip really uses it, with a few things to keep in mind:
    32	
    33	- **Blur** and **Invert** are included, and so is any [matte](/canvas/matte-tracks/) cutting the clip.
    34	- The clip's **Strength** isn't applied. A clip at 50 % still draws white where it's fully selected.
    35	- Layers in front of the clip are left out, so a title on top doesn't hide the selection.
    36	- The preview is black whenever the clip isn't on the frame, such as when the playhead is outside it.
    37	- With no range turned on, the qualifier picks everything, so the whole frame is white. With **Invert** on as well, it's black.
    38	
    39	## The Selection tag
    40	
    41	A **Selection** tag shows in the preview's top-left corner while the switch is on. It sits beside the **Ungraded** tag, and moves into the corner when Show Ungraded is off. See [Preview tags](/timeline/preview/#preview-tags).
    42	
    43	## Which clip it shows
    44	
    45	Show Selection shows one clip at a time, the first selected adjustment clip.
    46	
    47	- Select a different adjustment clip and it moves to that one.
    48	- Select something else, or nothing, so that no adjustment clip is selected, and it turns off.
    49	
    50	## Preview only
    51	
    52	Show Selection changes this window's preview and the [Preview Window](/timeline/preview-window/), and nothing else. An export and **Save Frame…** never see it.
    53	
    54	It isn't an edit, so it makes no undo step and the project doesn't change. It belongs to the window and isn't saved, so a new window starts with it off. See [Grade view tools are never saved](/color/show-ungraded/#grade-view-tools-are-never-saved).
    55	
    56	## Good to know
    57	
    58	- [Scopes](/color/scopes/) read the preview's frame, so while Show Selection is on they measure the grey picture, not the graded one.
    59	- It can be on at the same time as [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/). The clips behind the adjustment clip then lose their grades, so the selection is worked out from their ungraded picture.
    60	
    61	## With an agent
    62	
    63	`render_frame` can draw an adjustment clip's selection as this same grey picture, for any frame, with the switch left alone. The switch itself never reaches the tool. Frame Job won't draw it unless the clip named is an adjustment clip in this project. See [Tools: rendering and export](/mcp/tools-render-and-export/).
    64	
    65	## Related
    66	
    67	- [Qualifiers](/color/qualifiers/)
    68	- [Pick from Canvas](/color/pick-from-canvas/)
    69	- [Adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/)
    70	- [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/)
=== show-ungraded
     1	---
     2	title: "Show Ungraded"
     3	description: "Switch the preview to the picture with no grade on it, for a quick before and after, without changing the project."
     4	---
     5	
     6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
     7	
     8	Show Ungraded is a before and after switch. It shows the preview as if no clip were graded, so you can check what your grade is doing against the picture you started from.
     9	
    10	<AtAGlance menu="View ▸ Show Ungraded" keys="⌃⌘U" tools="render_frame" />
    11	
    12	## Compare with the ungraded picture
    13	
    14	Press <kbd>⌃⌘U</kbd>, or choose **View ▸ Show Ungraded**. Press it again to go back to the graded picture. The menu item has a checkmark while it's on, and it's always available.
    15	
    16	While it's on, every clip's **Light**, **Color**, **Wheels**, **Curves** and **Look** are set to neutral in this window's preview and the [Preview Window](/timeline/preview-window/). That includes nested clips, clips in a [matte](/canvas/matte-tracks/) and [adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/), so the grade an adjustment clip puts on everything behind it goes too.
    17	
    18	The project doesn't change. It isn't an edit, and it makes no undo step.
    19	
    20	## The Ungraded tag
    21	
    22	An **Ungraded** tag shows in the preview's top-left corner while the switch is on, so you can't mistake the plain picture for your grade. See [Preview tags](/timeline/preview/#preview-tags).
    23	
    24	## What it leaves on
    25	
    26	Show Ungraded only takes away the grade. These aren't part of the grade, so they stay on:
    27	
    28	- A [camera-log conversion](/hdr/camera-log/) on the media. It's how the file is read, so turning it off wouldn't give you the true source.
    29	- Filters.
    30	- The [chroma key](/effects/chroma-key/).
    31	- Placement, and everything else about a clip, such as its opacity and blend mode.
    32	
    33	[Scopes](/color/scopes/) read the preview's frame, so they follow the switch and measure the ungraded picture.
    34	
    35	## Grade view tools are never saved
    36	
    37	Show Ungraded, [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/) and the [scopes](/color/scopes/) only change how this window shows the picture. Each belongs to the window, each is off in a new window, and nothing about them is saved.
    38	
    39	None of them reaches an export or **Save Frame…**, which always use the graded picture. The thumbnails in the [Look](/color/looks/) gallery ignore Show Ungraded too.
    40	
    41	## With an agent
    42	
    43	`render_frame` can draw a frame as if no clip were graded, with the switch left alone, and its answer says the frame has every grade removed. The switch itself never reaches the tool. See [Tools: rendering and export](/mcp/tools-render-and-export/).
    44	
    45	## Related
    46	
    47	- [Scopes](/color/scopes/)
    48	- [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/)
    49	- [The Color tab](/color/color-tab/)
    50	- [Show SDR Version](/hdr/show-sdr-version/)
=== scopes
     1	---
     2	title: "Scopes"
     3	description: "Open the Scopes panel beside the preview to measure the picture while you grade, with two slots that each show a waveform, parade, vectorscope or histogram."
     4	---
     5	
     6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
     7	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
     8	
     9	Scopes measure the picture while you grade, so you're not relying on your eyes or your display. The panel sits beside the preview and shows two scopes at once.
    10	
    11	<AtAGlance menu="View ▸ Scopes" keys="⌃⌘W" tools="render_frame" />
    12	
    13	<Shot
    14	  name="04b-preview-scopes.preview"
    15	  alt="The preview with the Scopes panel on its right. The top slot shows a Waveform with red clip marks and the readouts Highlights clipped 1.9 % and Shadows clipped 52.7 %. The bottom slot shows a Vectorscope with its six colour targets and 1×, 2× and 4× zoom cells. Both slots are captioned Rec. 709 · encoded."
    16	/>
    17	
    18	## Open the scopes
    19	
    20	Press <kbd>⌃⌘W</kbd>, or choose **View ▸ Scopes**. Do the same again to close the panel. The menu item has a checkmark while it's open, and it's always available.
    21	
    22	The panel is a fixed column 248 points wide, the full height of the preview pane, between the picture and the inspector. The picture shrinks to fit what's left, and takes the whole pane back when the panel closes. If the [Loudness Meter](/audio/loudness-meter/) is on too, its column sits between the picture and the scopes.
    23	
    24	The panel is off in every new window. Your scope choices and zooms last while the window is open, even if you close and reopen the panel, and they aren't saved.
    25	
    26	## Choose a scope for each slot
    27	
    28	The panel has two slots, one above the other. Each has a pop-up at its top left that picks one of four scopes. A new window opens on **Waveform** over **Vectorscope**.
    29	
    30	| Scope | What it shows |
    31	| --- | --- |
    32	| [Waveform](/color/waveform-and-parade/#read-the-waveform) | Brightness across the frame, left to right. |
    33	| [Parade](/color/waveform-and-parade/#read-the-rgb-parade) | Red, green and blue as three waveforms side by side. |
    34	| [Vectorscope](/color/vectorscope/) | Hue and saturation, with colour targets and the skin line. |
    35	| [Histogram](/color/histogram/) | How many pixels sit at each level, per colour. |
    36	
    37	You can put the same scope in both slots. Each slot keeps its own vectorscope zoom, so two vectorscopes can show the picture at different zooms.
    38	
    39	## Read a slot's caption
    40	
    41	A faint caption at each slot's top right says what the scope is reading.
    42	
    43	| Project | Waveform and Parade | Vectorscope and Histogram |
    44	| --- | --- | --- |
    45	| SDR | Rec. 709 · encoded | Rec. 709 · encoded |
    46	| HDR (HLG) | HLG · cd/m² | Rec. 2100 HLG |
    47	
    48	"Encoded" means the scope reads the picture's stored values, not the light they stand for. An HDR project also changes the scales and targets. See [Scopes in an HDR project](/hdr/hdr-scopes/).
    49	
    50	## When the pane is short
    51	
    52	Waveform and Parade like a height of 200 points, Vectorscope a square of 224 points and Histogram 140 points. If the preview pane can't hold both slots at those sizes, they shrink together by the same proportion, and a vectorscope stays square and centred.
    53	
    54	Below a pane height of 360 points, only the top slot shows. The bottom slot comes back, with its pick, when there's room again.
    55	
    56	## What the scopes measure
    57	
    58	The scopes measure the frames the preview composes. They follow the picture live while it plays, jumping to the newest frame if they fall behind, and update after each edit while it's paused. Until a frame has been measured, a slot is empty and its readouts show "—". The scopes only run while the panel is open, so they cost nothing when it's closed.
    59	
    60	They read the whole frame, so the project's background counts as part of the picture. A black background beside a smaller clip shows up as shadows at level 0.
    61	
    62	Because they read the preview's frame, they follow what the preview is showing:
    63	
    64	- With [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/) on, they measure the ungraded picture. In an HDR project they keep their HLG reading.
    65	- With [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/) on, they measure the grey selection picture.
    66	- With [Show SDR Version](/hdr/show-sdr-version/) on in an HLG project, they measure the SDR picture exactly as in an SDR project, and switch to the Rec. 709 caption and targets.
    67	
    68	## With an agent
    69	
    70	No agent tool drives the panel. Instead, `render_frame` measures any of the four scopes on any frame, counting exactly as the panel does. Its answer gives the figures in words, such as the clipping percentages, and a JSON file next to the image holds the counts. If the measurement can't run, the frame is still written and the tool says the scopes couldn't be measured. See [Tools: rendering and export](/mcp/tools-render-and-export/).
    71	
    72	## Related
    73	
    74	- [Waveform and RGB Parade](/color/waveform-and-parade/)
    75	- [Vectorscope](/color/vectorscope/)
    76	- [Histogram](/color/histogram/)
    77	- [Scopes in an HDR project](/hdr/hdr-scopes/)
    78	- [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/)
=== waveform-and-parade
     1	---
     2	title: "Waveform and RGB Parade"
     3	description: "Read brightness and each colour channel across the frame, and find where highlights and shadows clip."
     4	---
     5	
     6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
     7	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
     8	
     9	The Waveform shows how bright the picture is across the frame. The Parade shows the same thing for red, green and blue separately. Both tell you where the picture is clipping, which is hard to judge by eye.
    10	
    11	<AtAGlance
    12	  menu="View ▸ Scopes"
    13	  keys="⌃⌘W"
    14	  where="A slot's pop-up in the Scopes panel ▸ Waveform or Parade"
    15	  tools="render_frame"
    16	/>
    17	
    18	<Shot
    19	  name="04b-preview-scopes.preview"
    20	  alt="The Waveform in the top slot of the Scopes panel beside the preview: a dark well labelled 0, 50 and 100 at its left, with a white trace, red marks along its top and bottom edges, and under it the readouts Highlights clipped 1.9 % and Shadows clipped 52.7 %."
    21	/>
    22	
    23	To open them, see [Scopes](/color/scopes/). In an HDR project they read differently, and [Scopes in an HDR project](/hdr/hdr-scopes/) has the scale.
    24	
    25	## Read the waveform
    26	
    27	The Waveform plots the picture's luma (Y′, its brightness). Left to right in the scope is left to right across the frame, and height is brightness, with black at the bottom and white at the top.
    28	
    29	Lines mark 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100 %, with 0, 50 and 100 labelled at the left. The trace is white on a near-black well in both light and dark appearance. The brighter a point in the trace, the more pixels sit there, on a log scale, so a level only a few pixels reach still shows.
    30	
    31	## Read the RGB parade
    32	
    33	The Parade shows red, green and blue as three waveforms side by side, in that order, each tinted its own colour. Each one works like the Waveform, with the same lines and the whole width of the frame.
    34	
    35	Use it to see a colour cast. Something that should be neutral grey sits at the same height in all three, and a channel sitting higher or lower is pulling the picture toward or away from that colour. **Temperature** and **Tint** in [Light](/color/light/), and the [wheels](/color/wheels/), are the usual ways to bring them back in line.
    36	
    37	## Find clipping
    38	
    39	A pixel clips high at the top level, where an 8-bit file would write 255, and low at the bottom level, where it would write 0. Detail at those levels has gone flat.
    40	
    41	**Clip marks** are red marks on the top and bottom edges of the scope. A mark sits over every column where at least 0.5 % of the pixels clip, on the top edge for highlights and the bottom edge for shadows, so you can see where in the frame it's happening. The Parade marks each channel on its own, so one channel can clip when the others don't.
    42	
    43	**Readouts** under the Waveform give the share of the whole frame, for example **Highlights clipped 1.8 %** and **Shadows clipped 52.7 %**. They show "—" until a frame has been measured. The [Histogram](/color/histogram/) has the same two readouts. The Parade and the Vectorscope have none.
    44	
    45	The readouts count everything in the frame. A black background around a smaller clip counts as clipped shadows, so a high figure may not be a problem with your footage. To bring highlights down, try **Exposure** or **Highlights** in [Light](/color/light/).
    46	
    47	## With an agent
    48	
    49	`render_frame` measures a frame's Waveform or Parade without the panel. Its answer says what share of pixels clips high and low, and for the Parade it gives that for each channel, which the panel doesn't show as a number. A JSON file next to the image holds the raw counts, the clip marks and the clipping figures. See [Tools: rendering and export](/mcp/tools-render-and-export/).
    50	
    51	## Related
    52	
    53	- [Scopes](/color/scopes/)
    54	- [Vectorscope](/color/vectorscope/)
    55	- [Histogram](/color/histogram/)
    56	- [Scopes in an HDR project](/hdr/hdr-scopes/)
    57	- [Light](/color/light/)
